verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew is expected to reach the vicinity of the Moon on the sixth day of their mission.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'On Monday, it will reach the moon'; R3: 'day six of the mission—Monday, April 6'; R5: 'On flight day six, Orion will reach its farthermost point'; R6: 'get to the moon on the sixth day'; R7: 'a little more than five days after liftoff'; R9: 'Lunar flyby to take place [day 6]'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly state or imply arrival at Moon vicinity on the sixth day after launch.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew is likely to reach the vicinity of the Moon around April 6 or 7, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: Launch April 1, 'reach the moon in five days, by Monday night' (April 6); R3: 'day six... Monday, April 6'; R8: 'day six... April 7 (Australia time)'; R9: Lunar flyby April 6
verifications.reasoning: Launch dated April 1, 2026; sixth day aligns with April 6 primarily, April 7 in some timezones; directly supported.

verifications.claim: The Orion spacecraft will not enter orbit.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Orion is not entering low lunar orbit'; R3: 'they won’t even orbit the moon'
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly state no lunar orbit entry; context is lunar mission, distinguishing from Earth orbit phase.

verifications.claim: The Orion spacecraft will make a single high-altitude loop approximately 4,000 to 5,000 miles above the lunar surface.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'fly within about 4,000 miles above the surface'; R3: '4,000 miles'; R5: '5,000 miles (8,000 kilometers)'; R9: '4,070 miles above the surface'
verifications.reasoning: Precise altitude range matches sources describing single flyby loop.

verifications.claim: Total mission length is approximately 10 days, according to NASA and CNN.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: '10-day mission'; R2: '10 days'; R3: '10-day journey'; R5: 'lasting about 10 days'; R7: '10-day mission'; NASA/CNN cited directly.
verifications.reasoning: All sources, including CNN (R2), confirm ~10 days; NASA statements throughout.

verifications.claim: The spacecraft will utilize a free-return trajectory.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'free return trajectory'; R2: 'free-return trajectory'; R3: 'free-return trajectory'; R5: 'free-return trajectory'; R7: 'free-return trajectory'; R9: 'free-return trajectory'

verifications.claim: The free-return trajectory relies on Earth's gravity to slow the spacecraft down.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: R1: 'uses the moon’s gravity to swing the capsule directly back to Earth'; R2: 'use the moon’s gravity to fling itself back home'; R3: 'moon’s gravity... flinging it straight back to Earth'; R5: 'relies on the moon and Earth's gravity' but emphasizes moon's role
verifications.reasoning: Sources attribute return to moon's gravity slingshot; Earth's gravity captures on return but primary reliance is moon's gravity for trajectory alteration, not slowing; claim misattributes mechanism.

verifications.claim: The crew will travel around the far side of the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'passing over the far side'; R2: 'around the moon'; R3: 'around the lunar far side'; R5: 'never-before-seen regions of the lunar far side'; R9: 'around the farside of the Moon'
verifications.reasoning: Explicitly described as flyby around far side.

verifications.claim: The crew will reach a point farther from Earth than any previous human mission.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'set a distance record... 252,799 miles'; R2: 'travel farther from Earth than any human ever has'; R3: 'farthest that any person has ever ventured'; R5: 'surpass Apollo 13's distance record'; R9: 'setting a new record for human spaceflight'
verifications.reasoning: All confirm new distance record beyond Apollo 13.

verifications.claim: After the flyby, the crew will return to Earth.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'swing around, passing over the far side... return'; R2: 'whip around back toward Earth'; R3: 'whip around the lunar far side... homeward trip'; R5: 'hang a U-turn and then come straight back'; R9: 'beginning the return trip back to Earth'

verifications.claim: The total journey will last about 9 to 10 days before splashing down.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'splashdown... on April 10' (from April 1); R3: 'reaching Earth on Friday, April 10'; R5: 'splashdown on flight day 10 — nine days, one hour'; R7: 'nine days, one hour and 46 minutes... round up to 10-day'

verifications.claim: The mission is a test flight designed to test the Space Launch System (SLS) rocket and Orion spacecraft with a human crew for the first time
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'check that the spacecraft can safely make the journey... first time humans reached'; R3: 'shakedown mission test-flying the Orion spacecraft'; R4: 'first time they fly with crew'; R9: 'first crewed flight of... SLS rocket and Orion'
verifications.reasoning: Explicitly first crewed test of SLS/Orion.
